title: Chat Control 1.0 interim derogation (Regulation (EU) 2021/1232) adopted
summary: The temporary derogation from the ePrivacy Directive was adopted, entering into force 2 August 2021 and originally valid until 3 August 2024, allowing providers to voluntarily detect, report and remove CSAM ('Chat Control 1.0').

title: European Commission proposes the CSA Regulation (CSAR)
summary: Commissioner Ylva Johansson presented the proposal for a Regulation to prevent and combat child sexual abuse (COM(2022) 209 final), procedure 2022/0155(COD), the permanent 'Chat Control 2.0' framework.

title: LIBE Committee adopts negotiating position removing indiscriminate scanning
summary: Parliament's Civil Liberties Committee (LIBE), rapporteur Javier Zarzalejos, adopted its report on the CSAR removing mandatory indiscriminate 'chat control' scanning and excluding end-to-end encrypted communications.

title: Interim derogation extended to 3 April 2026
summary: Following a provisional agreement of 15 February 2024, Parliament (10 April 2024) and Council (29 April 2024) approved extending the Chat Control 1.0 derogation until 3 April 2026, pending adoption of the permanent CSAR.

title: Trilogue negotiations on the permanent CSAR begin
summary: Interinstitutional trilogue negotiations on the permanent CSA Regulation ('Chat Control 2.0') commenced, with the file described officially as 'close to adoption'.

title: European Parliament rejects extension of Chat Control 1.0 by one vote
summary: In a voting thriller, Amendment 34 to Regulation (EU) 2021/1232 (extending its application period) carried 307 for : 306 against : 24 abstentions (637 cast); the plenary then declined to extend the derogation (reported 311 against : 228 in favour : 92 abstentions), letting the interim regime lapse.

title: Chat Control 1.0 interim scanning regime expires
summary: With no extension adopted, the temporary ePrivacy derogation (Regulation (EU) 2021/1232) expired on 4 April 2026, removing the legal basis platforms had relied on for voluntary CSAM scanning.

title: Council Legal Service warns proposal breaches Article 7 of the Charter
summary: The Council's own Legal Service opined that the 'voluntary' scanning still constitutes generalised scanning of communications, incompatible with Article 7 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights absent reasonable suspicion and prior judicial authorisation, and likely to be struck down by the CJEU.

title: COREPER ambassadors agree to revive temporary scanning extension
summary: EU ambassadors, on a proposal from the Cypriot Council presidency, agreed to push forward a formally 'new' temporary regulation reviving the expired Chat Control 1.0 voluntary-scanning framework, just three months after Parliament rejected it.

title: Fifth (expected final) CSAR 2.0 trilogue collapses
summary: The fifth trilogue on the permanent CSA Regulation, announced as the last under the Cyprus presidency, produced no deal, collapsing over the Council's insistence on suspicionless scanning; negotiations were pushed to autumn.

title: Council adopts position on the 'new' temporary regulation
summary: The Council formally adopted, by written procedure, its first-reading position on the substantively identical 'new' regulation reviving Chat Control 1.0, sending it to Parliament for a second reading.

title: Parliament approves Rule 170 urgent procedure to fast-track the revival
summary: Backed by the EPP, MEPs voted 331 in favour : 304 against : 11 abstentions to apply the urgent procedure under Rule 170, scheduling a binding vote for 9 July and, because it is a second reading, requiring an absolute majority of 361 MEPs to reject or amend the Council text.

title: Europski parlament ne uspijeva odbaciti oživljavanje Chat Controla 1.0 — mjera prolazi do 2028.
summary: Prema službenom poimeničnom glasovanju (RCV, 'Proposition de rejet'), prijedlog za odbacivanje stajališta Vijeća dobio je 314 glasova ZA odbacivanje : 276 protiv : 17 suzdržanih (112 nije glasalo). Iako je većina prisutnih glasala za odbacivanje, nije dosegnut prag apsolutne većine od 361 pa stajalište Vijeća prolazi: dobrovoljni masovni nadzor privatnih poruka vraća se na snagu do 3. travnja 2028., uz simbolično izuzeće za enkriptiranu komunikaciju. (Dio hrvatskih medija ranije je izvijestio 276:286:30.) Pregovori o trajnoj CSA uredbi nastavljaju se u rujnu.
